 Order
This Criminal Original Petition has been filed to quash the proceedings in C.C.No.3386 of 2021 pending on the file of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Egmore, Chennai.
2. The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the marriage between the first petitioner and the defacto complainant/2nd respondent is admitted one.
But the 2nd petitioner Pakkiriammal and 3rd petitioner Ram Prabhu and 4th petitioner, Arivoli are not connected with the allegations of demanding of dowry as stated by the defacto complainant.
When the alleged occurrence took place at Chennai, on 01.05.2017 at about 11.30 am, they were residing at Cuddalore

In the reply notice,
there is no such allegations as against the petitioners with regard to demanding dowry from the defacto complainant.
Under these circumstances, false allegations had been raised by https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis the defacto complainant only for the purpose of criminal case.
Hence, seeks to quash the case .

3. The learned Government (Crl. Side) appearing for the first respondent and the learned counsel appearing for the 2 nd respondent/defacto complainant submitted that now, the case been ripe for trial and before the trail court, defacto complainant was examined as P.W.1 and the case is posted for cross examination.
4.
I have considered the matter in the light of the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and perused the materials on records.
5. On perusal of the final report, it reveals that the respondent police relied upon eight witnesses.

On perusal of the statement of the defacto complainant, it is seen that the defacto complainant had specifically stated that on 01.05.2017, at about 11.30 a.m., the 2 nd petitioner/Pakkiriammal, 3rd petitioner/Ram Prabhu, 4th petitioner/Arivoli came to her house and humiliated her and threatened that she should not live with her husband unless she got money and also four acre of land from her father.

Under these circumstances, though the petitioners are denying the allegation and no such https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis type of allegations had been mentioned in the reply notice, the fact has to be decided by the Trial Court by considering the evidence produced by the prosecution.

It does not meet the parameters laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the following cases:
(i) R.P.Kapur Vs. The State of Punjab reported in AIR 1960 SC 866 (ii) State of Haryana & Ors. Vs. Ch.Bhajan Lal & Ors. reported in AIR 1992 SC 604 M.S. Adhisankaran vs / on 11 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175069978/

Hence, I find no reason to quash the criminal proceedings and I find no merit in the criminal original petition and hence, it is liable to be dismissed.
6. Accordingly, this Criminal Original Petition is dismissed.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petitions are closed.
The Trial Court is directed to dispose the case within a period of four months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
